The cost of freedom
2014-12-16T00:00:00+06:00 | The Daily Star
https://www.thedailystar.net/the-cost-of-freedom-55326

When we think war, we think of victory or defeat. That is only natural but in every conflict in human history the first slain of the turmoil is humanity itself. Our independence came at a price and as Bengalis we must pay due homage to the lives lost and the lives that went through innumerable hardship in those 9 months of struggle. We are a rebellious lot. Although we witness a culmination of our defiance against tyranny in the events leading to 1971, the seeds of hunger for freedom were sown centuries before. This week Star Lifestyle, takes you down memory lane in search of our identity from the pages of history. We look at the price we paid for our hard earned freedom.

We start our retrospection with the Independent Sultans of Bengal, rulers of this land during the medieval times. Despite being non-Bengalis, they basked in the soils of Bengal and became mutinous of all central power. Through their interaction, there was a diffusion of the spirit of victory and of freedom from the locals.

But we also look at the events of the not too distant past. In 1971 over 10 million Bangladeshis moved to India, an exodus of historic proportions. The innocent lives and their struggle for survival in those nine month of struggle is a lesser known part of our history. Then on, we move to the genocide and the persecution of the Bengalis. And we also focus on the younger generation and how they perceive victory. With it comes the change in attitude towards the war itself as decades whiz past, the war becomes more remote. Where do we stand, when it comes to remembering our past and our heritage? We introspect about the younger generation and the split that is apparent in their attitude towards all that is Bangla and Bangladeshi.
